environment.os: Linux local plus GitHub Actions macOS/Windows/Linux runners

source_tree_definition: SHA-256 over sorted tracked and untracked paths plus a NUL separator, file bytes and a trailing NUL separator for each path, excluding .agents, .git, node_modules, .fallow, dist and out.
implementation: Made the benchmark contract assert linux-core-synthetic on Linux and non-linux-core-synthetic on other hosts while retaining the explicit external cross-platform disposition.
Normalized the seeded prior-note path with node:path basename so Windows absolute paths cannot be mistaken for vault-relative paths or rejected as reserved segments.

checks.result: The focused benchmark contract passed locally with 12 expectations.
Routine local gates passed with 152 tests and 821 expectations; the benchmark contract passed on the Linux host.
Strict changed-file Fallow audit passed with no issues in the benchmark script.
The first platform-aware assertion repair passed macOS/Linux but retained a Windows benchmark path failure; the failed attempt is preserved before the basename fix.
Quality run passed on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows after the assertion and platform-native path fixes; run URL https://github.com/ashutoshpw/open-obsidian/actions/runs/34592908501.
Desktop-build run passed packaging, release-manifest, runtime-notice and attribution audits on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows; run URL https://github.com/ashutoshpw/open-obsidian/actions/runs/34592908593.

limitations: The benchmark remains synthetic and release_eligible=false; pinned hardware, reference Obsidian vaults, Electron input-to-paint, long-running resource, human comparison and plugin/runtime certification remain pending.
The GitHub Actions green result proves the available matrix contract and packaging jobs, not reference-vault portability or human validation.
result: The available macOS, Windows and Linux quality and desktop-build matrix is green for the benchmark portability repair, while the external performance and reference-vault gates remain explicitly pending.
